```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(inferguidR)
```

This tutorial moves from an explicit question to a saved power specification.
It runs offline with the installed package. All design values are hypothetical;
a subject-matter justification of the effect and sampling design remains necessary.

## Describe the question

The advisor records explicit choices. It does not infer a study design from data.
At each step, inspect the available option identifiers before answering.

```{r advisor}
session <- advisor_session()
advisor_question(session)
session <- advisor_answer(session, "compare")
advisor_question(session)
```

The returned session is a new object. Keep it if you want to continue or return
to an earlier answer. A partially answered session is not a completed analysis
recommendation. `advisor_save()` and `advisor_restore()` support a longer session;
review any script from `advisor_r_code()` before executing it.

## Make the assumptions explicit

For the calculation below, assume two independent normal populations with equal
variances, equal allocation, and a prespecified standardised mean difference of
0.5. These assumptions select the pooled-variance two-sample t procedure. They
do not describe paired, clustered or unequal-variance observations.

```{r specification}
spec <- analysis_spec(
  "t_means_two_independent", "a_priori",
  inputs = list(alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80, d = 0.5),
  options = list(tails = "two")
)
spec
```

`alpha` is the two-sided type-I error probability; `power` is the target rejection
probability under the specified alternative. The effect size is the difference
in population means divided by their common standard deviation. An a priori
specification asks the solver for sample size, so do not also supply `n_total`.

## Inspect the result before using it

```{r solve}
result <- solve_design(spec)
result
stopifnot(result$status$code == "ok")
result$group_sizes
result$assumptions
result$warnings
result$validation
```

`solved$n_total` is the combined sample size; `group_sizes` gives the allocation.
`achieved$power` can exceed the target because only admissible integer designs
are considered. The `ok` calculation status and the method's reference-validation
status answer different questions. Neither establishes clinical utility or
correct study assumptions.

## Check an invalid request

Constructor errors and numerical outcomes are distinct. Here the error is
expected because a probability is outside its domain.

```{r invalid-input}
problem <- tryCatch(
  analysis_spec("t_means_two_independent", "a_priori",
    inputs = list(alpha = 1.5, power = 0.8, d = 0.5)),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
problem
stopifnot(is.character(problem))
```

For other analysis modes use `calculate_power()`. Inspect `?analysis_spec` for
mode-specific targets and `list_methods()` for available procedures; a registry
entry alone does not establish that a numerical engine is implemented.

## Save a specification and verify its round trip

```{r round-trip}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
writeLines(ig_to_json(spec), path)
restored <- ig_from_json(file = path)
stopifnot(identical(ig_hash(spec), ig_hash(restored)))
replayed <- solve_design(restored)
stopifnot(identical(result$solved, replayed$solved))
```

Save the result as well as its specification when archiving an analysis. Record
the package revision and execution environment: a matching content hash proves
identity of that content, not scientific validation across software versions.

## Continue

The [classification tutorial](classification.html) introduces denominators and
explicit operating points. To explore the same public functions interactively:

```{r workbench, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("shiny", "ggplot2"))
launch_app()
```

The launch chunk is not evaluated during a documentation build because it starts
an interactive server. No external reference application is required.

```{r session-information}
sessionInfo()
```
